newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee off lows vs fwd dlr, RBI curbs spot.
newsitem.headline: India rupee off lows vs fwd dlr, RBI curbs spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee recovered from a weaker opening against the forward dollar, while in the spot market the rupee came off highs due to intermittent central bank dollar buying, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said sentiment pushed the rupee down against the forward dollar after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened in the spot market but forward dollar sales led to a rally to Monday's closing levels.
In latest deals, October-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 85/87 paise after touching 90 paise in opening deals, dealers said. October dollars ended Monday at 85/87 paise.
Some dealers said the RBI had bought forward dollars but were unable to confirm deals. Most dealers attributed the movement in forward premiums to sentiment generated by central bank intervention.

"Forward premiums rose briefly on sentiment when RBI bought spot dollars in the morning," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But later there was some selling of forward dollars and rates are back to yesterday's levels."
He said forward premiums would remain soft on easy domestic liquidity and expectations of low interest rates.
The RBI monetary policy issued on April 15 announced measures to lower deposit rates and has led to a cut in lending rates by several banks.
The end of a three-week political crisis, and appointment of Inder Kumar Gujral as the country's new prime minister has had no discernible influence on the market, dealers said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the RBI bought spot dollars betwen 35.76 and 35.77 as the rupee looked like appreciating above 35.75, dealers said.
"But their (RBI) buying has been sporadic," said another dealer. "At the moment the market is quiet again."
He said the rupee would continue to hold firm as dollar supplies were good and demand poor.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted at 35.762/772 rupees.
